newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi plans $300 mln airport expansion.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi plans $300 mln airport expansion.

text.p: Abu Dhabi has earmarked over 1.1 billion dirhams ($300 million) to expand its main airport by the year 2000, an official said in remarks published on Sunday.

Civil Aviation Chairman Sheikh Hamdan bin Mubarak al-Nahayan was quoted by the Emirates News daily as saying a second runway would be built at the capital's airport by 2000. It was expected to cost around 300 million dirhams.
Passenger terminal facilities would also be expanded at a cost of 500 million dirhams.

"These will include the construction of a satellite terminal building with a capacity to handle up to three million passengers a year, as well as a building consisting of 16 new bays for aircraft," the newspaper said.
The main airport in the United Arab Emirates' capital serves some 43 airlines and around four million passengers a year. It handles over 70,000 tonnes of cargo annually.
The Emirates News said the airport would extend cargo facilities, with three new warehouses planned at a cost of nine million dirhams.

Work was already underway to upgrade taxiways, extend cargo aprons, construct bays for wide-bodied planes, build new passenger lounges and install a new baggage handling system, it said. This was costing around 118 million dirhams.
Civil Aviation also plans a 60 million dirham project to build a hotel and golf course near the airport.
The newspaper said 35 million dirhams had already been spent on expanding the airport's catering facilities.
